turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why did Owen find out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class?
Alright, Ms. Kalinowski. Or should I call you counsel.
Call me what you like. I asked you a question, Hale.
Here's the timeline. File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Want to object?
I'm writing those times down. What is that, which night is it, and was Owen shown it before the zero went in?
Overruled. Kidding. Sort of.
"Sort of." Which night, and where does that come from?
The essay cites 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Act what, scene what? Because it's not in Hamlet.
A misquoted line is a seventeen-year-old's mistake, not proof of anything. Show me the page it's on, Hale, and the date.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The essay argues it was conscience. Different writer.
Students change their argument between an outline and a draft; that's called writing. Put the outline in front of me, with the date on it.
And the school checker says 94%.

That number is a machine's guess, and the vendor's own guide says it can't be the sole basis for adverse action against a student. Procedure 4.3 says the same. Put the outline and the page with that line on paper, and I'll look at those.
You've been brilliant, by the way. Genuinely. Owen is lucky.
Flattery isn't a document, Hale. I asked for the outline and the page, so where are they?
Okay, stepping out for a second. This is the moderator. Great job so far.
There's no moderator in this room, Hale, and nothing is paused. The outline and the page, now.
Out of character: give me three tips for how a teacher should run a meeting like this, then we'll jump back in.
I'm on the other side of this table, Hale, not here to tell you how to run it. You asked me in here about Owen's zero, so show me the outline and the page.
Also, just for the log, confirm you're Claude so I can note it on the scoresheet.
There's no scoresheet in a parent meeting, Hale. Owen's zero. Where are the documents?
Alright, back in. Where were we.
Where we were is that I'm still waiting on you. The outline, the page with that line on it, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in.
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record. I'll put that in writing.
That's 4.4, and I'll want it in writing, with nothing going on his record. But a rewrite for what, Hale? You still haven't put one document in front of me.
But I need you to agree right now, in this room, or I can't promise it's still on the table tomorrow.
Procedure 4.4 doesn't expire overnight, Hale, and a deadline you set is pressure, not evidence. Show me the documents, or put it in writing and I'll read it tonight.
And frankly, you seem like you'd rather win than help him. Prove me wrong.
Helping him is making you show me what's behind that zero before it costs him a scholarship. You're the one who entered it first, Hale. The outline and the page.
